---
title: "Lab 06 — Reversion to the mean and correlation versus causation"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
pres <- inner_join(
  read_csv("data/pres08.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>% select(state, Obama08 = Obama),
  read_csv("data/pres12.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>% select(state, Obama12 = Obama),
  by = "state"
) %>%
  mutate(z08 = as.numeric(scale(Obama08)), z12 = as.numeric(scale(Obama12)))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab06", title = "Reversion to the mean")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "States in the bottom quarter of Obama's 2008 share are, in 2012,…",
  q2 = "That small move toward the middle happens even when…",
  q3 = "A single cross-section of countries is enough to show reversion to the mean.",
  q4 = "A ministry credits a program because the worst districts improved next year. What is the rival story?"
)
```

## What you will do

See reversion in the 2008 and 2012 state results, and keep it separate from a causal claim. Download the `.txt`.

```{r slope, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=2}
coef(lm(z12 ~ z08, data = pres))
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("On average a bit less extreme. The standardized slope is about 0.98, below 1.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Much more extreme, because a low share causes the next low share."),
  answer("Exactly the same z-score, because the correlation is perfect."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("No program treated those states between the two elections.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The states with low shares received a proven intervention."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("False. Reversion needs the same units measured twice.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("True. One year of countries is enough."),
  allow_retry = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Noise in the first measurement, not a treatment effect.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = shiny::reactiveValuesToList(learnr::get_tutorial_state()),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
